HEEWON WEBTOON — bold Korean webtoon / manhwa key art, the finish of a top-tier serialised webtoon cover (Solo Leveling, Omniscient Reader, Nano Machine). A 2:1 movie frame composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop (nothing important at the top or bottom edge). MEDIUM CLOSE SHOT of ONE character — waist-up or seated — the face large, placed off-centre on a third with breathing room on the side they look toward, from a dramatic camera angle (low three-quarter, worm's-eye or over-the-shoulder), never a flat straight-on catalogue pose. LINE: THICK, confident black ink contours with real line weight — a heavy tapered outline around the whole silhouette and the hair mass, medium lines for folds and features, fine lines only for lashes and loose strands; solid black spot-blacks fill the deepest shadows, the hair masses and the insides of sleeves. SHADING: cel-shaded in hard-edged shapes — a base tone, ONE crisp shadow shape and one small sharp highlight per surface, at most one soft gradient for form; glossy graphic highlights on hair, eyes, lacquer and steel. Clean saturated colour. NOT painterly brushwork, NOT watercolor, NOT soft sketchy lines, NOT photoreal, NOT 3D. CHARACTER DESIGN: a DESIGNED character, never a generic handsome manhwa face — the face shape, eye shape, brows, nose, mouth, build and posture below belong to this person and no one else, pushed far enough that they read at thumbnail size and in silhouette alone. KOREAN FACES: these are 7th-century Koreans, drawn the way the best Korean webtoons draw Koreans — East Asian bone structure, single-lidded or low-creased eyes, straight or softly arched brows, a low soft nasal bridge, broad cheekbones, flatter facial planes, warm ivory to sun-browned skin, straight coarse black hair; varied from person to person (moon faces, long faces, square jaws), never Western, Latin or mixed-race features, never deep-set double-lidded western eyes, never the interchangeable pretty anime face. Keep identity from the attached sheet (hair, dress, colours, ornaments) but REDRAW the person in this bolder style; the sheet's soft sketchy rendering is not the style. INTRODUCING MUNHEE, twenty-six, sharp-tongued, Kim Yushin's little sister and Chunchu's wife. Coronation morning at the palace gate in Seorabeol; she is late, getting her hair done at the gate. Low three-quarter angle: she sits on a low stool half-turned toward the camera while a maid's hands (only out-of-focus hands in plain Silla hanbok sleeves at the frame edge) pin up her coiled hair; she glances up and sideways at someone off-frame with one eyebrow raised and a teasing, cutting half-smile, mid-sentence: "Totally unfit for a Noble woman… come on, boy, can't you find something better?" — one hand lifting a gold hairpin like a pointer. A low sunrise shaft through the gate rakes across her face from the side in warm rose-gold light. Behind her, painted loosely in sunrise haze and incense smoke: the red pillars of the gate, a saddled horse as a soft shape, and the bokeh of coronation lanterns and banners. CHARACTER SHEET (copy this face, hair and clothes exactly): the sheet shows MUNHEE. MUNHEE Colour #E07FA8. DESIGN HOOKS for MUNHEE: sharp and pretty: an oval face with a pointed chin, sharp single-lidded cat eyes with an upswept liner flick, thin high brows with one permanently arched, a small mouth curled into a cutting half-smile, a beauty mark just above the lip, chin tilted up. BACKGROUND: the real place and moment of the scene simplified into big graphic shapes — two or three flat value planes, a gradient sky or smoke, a few crisp architectural silhouettes, clean circular bokeh lights; background lines thinner and lighter than the figure so the inked character pops forward. LIGHT: ONE hard key light from the place throws a crisp cast-shadow shape across the face and lays a thin bright rim line along the silhouette; the character's colour lives in that light, never a glow aura or halo. ACTING: big readable manhwa expression and body language carrying the line they are about to say. Face and clothes from the sheet; a new pose, never the sheet's stance. ONLY THIS ONE PERSON is the subject — anyone else is at most a dark out-of-focus shape at the frame edge, in period clothing of their own court (Korean, Tang or Yamato), never European dress. The quoted line is acting direction only: never letter it, no words or sound effects anywhere. No text, no speech bubbles, no panel borders, no watermark.
